docs.title: About
docs.text: Structs.sh is an interactive data structure and algorithm visualiser and educational platform for computer science students.

docs.title: Algorithm Visualiser
docs.text:
Interactive animated visualisations of classic data structures and algorithms, including (but not limited to):

  • Linked Lists
  • Binary Search Trees
  • AVL Trees
  • Graphs (in progress!)

docs.title: Visual Debugger
docs.text:
• Debug and visualise data structures in your own C code.
  • Currently supports linked lists.

docs.title: Why Structs.sh?
docs.text:
Structs.sh aims to be a comprehensive educational resource for data structures and algorithms, developed by passionate computer science and engineering students at UNSW.

The project was inspired by Tactile-DS, a tutoring tool and reference implementation developed in 2020 for COMP2521.

Structs.sh exists to bridge the gap between a student's high-level understanding of computer science concepts and how those concepts translate into real code. It was started by students who felt there was a lack of tools that help build strong visual intuition for algorithmic thinking.

docs.title: Contributing to Structs.sh
docs.text:
Before you begin

Feel free to use your preferred LLM to help along the way — the guidelines below are intentionally concise!

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
• Clone the repository and install the development dependencies:
git clone git@github.com:devsoc-unsw/structs.sh.git structs
cd structs
npm install
  • Start the project locally:
docker compose up --build

docs.title: Contribution models
docs.text: There are two ways to contribute to Structs.sh:

docs.title: Subcommittee members
docs.text:
• Follow GitHub's shared repository model.
  • Use Conventional Branch when naming branches.
  • Discuss ideas, questions, or ongoing work in the internal Discord server.

docs.title: External contributors
docs.text:
• Follow GitHub's fork and pull model.
  • If you need a hand, open a help wanted issue or contact us.
